summary_plain: This ground-based investigation developed advanced computer models to study how flames spread across solid materials like plastics and wax in microgravity. By comparing model predictions with spaceflight experiment images, researchers aimed to better understand material flammability limits. This work improves our ability to predict fire risks and protect spacecraft environments.
summary_expert: The investigation developed and validated an unsteady flamelet generated manifold (UFGM) modeling framework to simulate concurrent flame spread in microgravity. Researchers evaluated flat sheets, spheres, and rod-shaped polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) samples as well as wax cylinders across various BASS geometries. Experimental imagery from BASS and BASS-II was post-processed using two-color tomography methods to reconstruct 3D soot and temperature fields, serving as benchmark evaluation metrics alongside flame geometry, temperature distribution, soot volume fraction, and flame spread rate.
